### Synthesis Overview

The PR adds an integration test to verify that five direct-generation prompts do not produce tool-calling narration, updates CLI dispatch test assertions to include the new `prompt=None` default, reformats two source files, and deletes the stale `.opencode/` directory and `opencode.json`. The three models reviewed commit `72dce56`; a follow-up commit (`3b2baaa`) on the same branch subsequently resolved the majority of reported findings (standard fixture adoption, standard imports, model environment variable, and missing prompt dispatch test). The remaining outstanding issues are stale documentation and agent-instruction references to the deleted `.opencode/` tree, and a missing unit test for `_cmd_run`'s internal `_apply_prompt` branch. No Critical or correctness bugs were identified.

```
[M-W-01] Integration test bypasses suite-standard `llm_available` fixture
Severity: Warning
Category: Testing
File: tests/integration/test_prompt_verification.py
Lines: 72–80 (in commit 72dce56)
Detail: Kimi and GLM both identified that the original test defined a local
`require_lm_studio` autouse fixture using `httpx` against a hardcoded
`http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` URL. This diverged from the project-standard
`llm_available` fixture in `tests/integration/conftest.py`, which uses `requests`,
honours the `LLM_API_BASE` environment variable, and applies a 10-second timeout.
The custom fixture created inconsistent skip behaviour and added an unnecessary
`httpx` dependency.
Models: Kimi ✓ Qwen ✗ GLM ✓
Dissenting view: Qwen considered the custom fixture acceptable and marked it
as passing in the Phase-5 testing checklist.
Suggestion: Replace the local fixture with `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("llm_available")`
on the test class.
Status: Resolved in HEAD by follow-up commit 3b2baaa.
```

```

```
[M-S-02] Hardcoded model name in integration test
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Testing
File: tests/integration/test_prompt_verification.py
